part.text: I’m treating “night” as 7 p.m.–5:59 a.m. and “day” as 6 a.m.–6:59 p.m. The data can compare reported crash frequency and injury/fatal-crash severity, but it has no traffic or travel exposure data to establish risk per trip.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: generate_options.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+con = duckdb.connect()
+source = "read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')"
+summary = con.execute(
+    f"""
+    WITH timed AS (
+      SELECT *, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) AS hour
+      FROM {source}
+    ), grouped AS (
+      SELECT
+        CASE WHEN hour >= 19 OR hour < 6 THEN 'Night (7pm–5:59am)'
+             ELSE 'Day (6am–6:59pm)' END AS period,
+        COUNT(*) AS crashes,
+        COUNT(number_of_persons_injured) AS crashes_with_known_injury_count,
+        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_persons_injured > 0) AS injury_crashes,
+        COUNT(number_of_persons_killed) AS crashes_with_known_killed_count,
+        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_persons_killed > 0) AS fatal_crashes
+      FROM timed
+      GROUP BY 1
+    )
+    SELECT * FROM grouped
+    """
+).df()
+days = con.execute(
+    f"SELECT date_diff('day', min(crash_date), max(crash_date)) + 1 FROM {source}"
+).fetchone()[0]
+order = ["Day (6am–6:59pm)", "Night (7pm–5:59am)"]
+summary["period"] = pd.Categorical(summary["period"], categories=order, ordered=True)
+summary = summary.sort_values("period").reset_index(drop=True)
+hours = {order[0]: 13, order[1]: 11}
+summary["calendar_days_in_date_range"] = days
+summary["clock_hours_per_day"] = summary["period"].astype(str).map(hours)
+summary["period_clock_hours"] = summary["calendar_days_in_date_range"] * summary["clock_hours_per_day"]
+summary["crashes_per_clock_hour"] = summary["crashes"] / summary["period_clock_hours"]
+summary["injury_crashes_pct"] = 100 * summary["injury_crashes"] / summary["crashes_with_known_injury_count"]
+summary["fatal_crashes_per_100k"] = 100_000 * summary["fatal_crashes"] / summary["crashes_with_known_killed_count"]
+
+colors = ["#4472C4", "#E07A32"]
+labels = ["Day", "Night"]
+
+def save_bar(values, filename, ylabel, title, formatter, value_label):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.6))
+    bars = ax.bar(labels, values, color=colors, width=0.58)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_title(title, pad=13)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[formatter(v) for v in values], padding=5, fontsize=10)
+    ax.margins(y=0.2)
+    fig.text(0.5, 0.015, value_label, ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#555555")
+    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 1])
+    fig.savefig(OUT / filename, dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+day = summary.iloc[0]
+night = summary.iloc[1]
+
+v1 = summary[["period", "crashes", "calendar_days_in_date_range", "clock_hours_per_day", "period_clock_hours", "crashes_per_clock_hour"]].copy()
+v1["period"] = v1["period"].astype(str)
+v1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+save_bar(
+    summary["crashes_per_clock_hour"].tolist(),
+    "option_1.png",
+    "Police-reported crashes per clock-hour",
+    "Crash frequency by clock-time window",
+    lambda x: f"{x:.1f}",
+    f"Night = 7pm–5:59am; day = 6am–6:59pm. Date range: {days} calendar days.",
+)
+
+v2 = summary[["period", "injury_crashes", "crashes_with_known_injury_count", "injury_crashes_pct"]].copy()
+v2["period"] = v2["period"].astype(str)
+v2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+save_bar(
+    summary["injury_crashes_pct"].tolist(),
+    "option_2.png",
+    "Crashes involving injury (%)",
+    "Share of crashes with an injury",
+    lambda x: f"{x:.1f}%",
+    "Denominator: crashes with a reported (non-missing) injury count.",
+)
+
+v3 = summary[["period", "fatal_crashes", "crashes_with_known_killed_count", "fatal_crashes_per_100k"]].copy()
+v3["period"] = v3["period"].astype(str)
+v3.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+save_bar(
+    summary["fatal_crashes_per_100k"].tolist(),
+    "option_3.png",
+    "Fatal crashes per 100,000 crashes",
+    "Share of crashes involving a death",
+    lambda x: f"{x:.1f}",
+    "Denominator: crashes with a reported (non-missing) killed count.",
+)
+
+rate_lift_injury = night["injury_crashes_pct"] / day["injury_crashes_pct"] - 1
+rate_ratio_fatal = night["fatal_crashes_per_100k"] / day["fatal_crashes_per_100k"]
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Police-reported crash frequency per clock-hour",
+            "denominator": "Clock-hours in each period across the inclusive date range",
+            "grouping": "Night (7pm–5:59am) vs day (6am–6:59pm)",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Normalizing by clock-hours makes crash frequency comparable despite the unequal lengths of the two time windows.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"The data records {night['crashes_per_clock_hour']:.1f} police-reported crashes per clock-hour at night versus {day['crashes_per_clock_hour']:.1f} by day, so reported crash frequency is lower at night under these clock-time definitions.",
+            "interpretation": "This compares when police-reported crashes occur, with counts normalized for the different durations of the night and day windows. It is a defensible frequency comparison, but it cannot establish risk per trip or person because traffic and travel exposure by hour are not in the data.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Share of crashes involving at least one injury",
+            "denominator": "Crashes with a non-missing number_of_persons_injured",
+            "grouping": "Night (7pm–5:59am) vs day (6am–6:59pm)",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "The share of crashes with an injury compares harmful outcomes conditional on a crash, rather than simply comparing crash counts.",
+            "probability": 0.45,
+            "answer": f"{night['injury_crashes_pct']:.1f}% of night crashes involved an injury, compared with {day['injury_crashes_pct']:.1f}% of day crashes (about {rate_lift_injury:.0%} higher at night).",
+            "interpretation": "This answers whether a reported crash is more likely to involve injury at night, using crashes with known injury counts as the denominator. It shows a higher injury-crash share at night, but it does not measure the chance of injury per journey or account for differences in who or how many people are traveling.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Fatal crashes per 100,000 crashes",
+            "denominator": "Crashes with a non-missing number_of_persons_killed",
+            "grouping": "Night (7pm–5:59am) vs day (6am–6:59pm)",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Fatal-crash frequency per crash highlights the most severe recorded outcome while adjusting for the different number of crashes in each period.",
+            "probability": 0.30,
+            "answer": f"There were {night['fatal_crashes_per_100k']:.1f} fatal crashes per 100,000 night crashes versus {day['fatal_crashes_per_100k']:.1f} per 100,000 day crashes (about {rate_ratio_fatal:.1f} times as high at night).",
+            "interpretation": "This compares the proportion of crashes involving at least one death among crashes with a known killed count, so it addresses crash severity rather than crash volume. The fatal-crash share is higher at night, but this cannot show fatality risk per road user or travel distance without exposure data.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+print(summary.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Date span days: {days}")
*** End Patch
